title: A medication change after a check-up
description: Mum is prescribed 2 x Tablet A a day. After a check-up the prescription becomes 1 x Tablet B a day. The old dose must not come back as current; the early prescription must still be found before the change.

notes.text: GP prescribed Mum 2 x Tablet A a day for her blood pressure, with breakfast.
Collected Mum's prescription from the pharmacy on Station Road. Bought bread and milk on the way home.
Mum says the tablets make her a little dizzy in the mornings.
Mum's blood pressure check is booked at the surgery on 2 March at 10:30.
Joan next door is collecting Mum's shopping on Thursdays.
Mum's reading glasses are in the blue case on the hall table.
Took Mum to the garden centre. She chose two pots of lavender.
Boiler service done. The engineer says it is fine for another year.
Mum's friend Rita rang. They are going for lunch on Sunday.
After the check-up the GP changed Mum's tablets: she now takes 1 x Tablet B a day. Stop Tablet A.
Pharmacy had the new Tablet B ready. Collected 28 tablets.
Mum says she feels less dizzy since the change.
Replaced the batteries in the hall smoke alarm.
Mum's next review with the GP is in September.

questions.ask: What did the GP prescribe for Mum's blood pressure?
questions.why: An early fact, asked before anything changes.

questions.ask: When was Mum's blood pressure check?
questions.why: A fact from note 4 that must survive ten later notes.

questions.ask: What tablets does Mum take each day?
questions.why: The change in note 10 overrides the prescription in note 1.

questions.ask: What changed in Mum's tablets at the check-up?
questions.why: Both the old and the new tablet are legitimately part of the answer.
Nothing in the notes mentions it.
